variables.title: Variables
variables.notes: Variables are assigned using the leftward arrow (←). APL is dynamically typed.

data_types.title: Data Types
data_types.code:
int ← 42
float ← 3.14
char ← 'a'
str ← 'hello'
bool ← 1  ⍝ Booleans are represented as 0 and 1
complex ← 1j2
data_types.notes: APL supports integers, floats, complex numbers, and characters. Strings are character arrays.

operators.title: Operators
operators.notes: APL uses Unicode symbols for mathematical and logical operations. Operations are evaluated strictly right-to-left.

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.code:
x ← 10
res ← { ⍵>0: 'Positive' ⋄ ⍵<0: 'Negative' ⋄ 'Zero' } x

⍝ Alternatively, using control structures in traditional functions:
:If x>0
    res2 ← 'Positive'
:Else
    res2 ← 'Non-positive'
:EndIf
conditionals.notes: Dfn guards (:) evaluate to the right side if the condition on the left is true. Control structures like :If/:Else are used in dfns or tradfns.

for_loop.title: For Loop
for_loop.code:
⍝ Implicit looping (Array orientation)
squares ← {⍵×⍵}¨ ⍳5

⍝ Explicit looping (Tradfn/Control Structures)
:For i :In ⍳5
    ⎕←i
:EndFor
for_loop.notes: Explicit loops are rare. The Each operator (¨) applies a function to each element of an array, which replaces most for-loops.

while_loop.title: While Loop
while_loop.notes: :While and :EndWhile execute a block of code as long as the condition evaluates to true (1).

functions.title: Functions
functions.code:
⍝ Dfn (Dynamic function)
Add ← {⍺ + ⍵}
res ← 3 Add 4

⍝ Tradfn (Traditional function)
∇ r ← x Multiply y
  r ← x × y
∇
functions.notes: Dfns use curly braces; ⍺ represents the left argument, ⍵ the right argument. Tradfns use the del symbol (∇).

arrays.title: Arrays
arrays.code:
vec ← 1 2 3 4 5
mat ← 2 3 ⍴ 1 2 3 4 5 6  ⍝ Reshape (⍴) into a 2x3 matrix
shape ← ⍴ mat            ⍝ Gets the shape: 2 3

firstElement ← ⊃vec      ⍝ First element
arrays.notes: APL is fundamentally about arrays. Elements are separated by spaces. The ⍴ operator constructs and queries dimensions.

maps.title: Maps
maps.code:
⍝ Namespaces are often used as dictionaries/maps in Dyalog APL
dict ← ⎕NS ''
dict.key1 ← 'value1'
dict.key2 ← 42

val ← dict.key1
maps.notes: Namespaces (created with ⎕NS) act as dynamic objects or maps to store key-value pairs.

error_handling.title: Error Handling
error_handling.code:
:Trap 0
    res ← 1 ÷ 0  ⍝ Intentional divide by zero
:Else
    ⎕←'An error occurred: ', ⎕EN
:EndTrap
error_handling.notes: :Trap catches specified error numbers (0 means all errors). ⎕EN holds the error number.

comments.title: Comments & Headers
comments.code:
# Comment in APL
# Multi-line comments or docstrings
# are documented here
comments.notes: APL uses # or language-specific delimiters (% in MATLAB, ! in Fortran) for comments.

numbers.title: Vectors, Matrices & Numbers
numbers.notes: APL is optimized for vector and matrix calculations with high-precision numerical representations.

booleans.title: Logical Vectors & Booleans
booleans.code:
is_valid = TRUE
flags = c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE)
booleans.notes: APL provides boolean types with support for element-wise vector logic operations.

type_casting.title: Type Coercion & Casting
type_casting.notes: APL converts data between numeric, character, factor, and logical representations.

strings.title: Strings & Character Vectors
strings.notes: APL treats strings as atomic character scalars or vector arrays.

string_formatting.title: String Formatting
string_formatting.notes: APL formats numerical output with sprintf formatting specifiers.

pattern_matching.title: Conditionals & Switches
pattern_matching.notes: APL executes branch logic via switch, ifelse, or conditional filtering.

range.title: Sequences & Indexing
range.notes: APL indexes matrices and vectors using 1-based indexing and sequence generators.

iterators.title: Vectorized Apply & Iteration
iterators.notes: APL emphasizes vectorized functional processing (apply, map) over explicit loops.

oop_classes.title: Object Systems & S3/S4
oop_classes.code:
# Object systems in APL
obj = list(name = "Model", score = 0.95)
class(obj) = "metric"
oop_classes.notes: APL uses class dispatch systems (S3/S4 in R, multiple dispatch in Julia) for data modeling.

lists.title: DataFrames & Lists
lists.notes: APL stores heterogeneous columnar records in data frames and lists.

tuples.title: Pairs & Records
tuples.notes: APL uses named vectors or lightweight structures for data records.

sets.title: Set Operations
sets.notes: APL provides native mathematical set functions (union, intersect, setdiff).

modules_import.title: Libraries & Packages
modules_import.notes: APL loads package namespaces using library or import declarations.
